prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 762px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 761px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 762px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact API reference for REST endpoints, used to locate an endpoint and confirm its HTTP method, auth requirement, rate limit, and behavior.","reading":"Readers scan the Endpoint column as the row anchor, glance across the short Method/Auth/Rate-limit fields for constraints, then read Description for behavior; comparison is mainly row-by-row rather than column-by-column.","groups":["Method, Auth, and Rate limit form a compact metadata cluster of short categorical/constraint values read together after the endpoint.","Endpoint and Description are the two wide semantic columns: Endpoint identifies the resource, Description explains what it does."],"keep_intact":["Endpoint paths, especially /api/v1/export/{jobId}/download","HTTP methods such as DELETE","Auth schemes such as Bearer","Rate-limit values such as 600/min"],"may_wrap":["Description sentences","Possibly the Rate limit header if a design needs a few extra pixels, but not its values"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[282,76,67,89,247],"idea":"Identifier-first and description-max: every endpoint and metadata value stays on one line, while Description receives all remaining width and wraps to about three lines."},{"name":"B","widths":[282,95,95,95,194],"idea":"Equal metadata band: Method, Auth, and Rate limit share equal widths for a clean vertical scan, accepting a narrower Description that wraps to about four lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[282,105,90,110,174],"idea":"Metadata-heavy scan: give the short constraint fields generous breathing room and let Description become the tall wrapping column, prioritizing quick method/auth/rate comparison over prose density."}]}
